# MathBoard

> MathBoard is an open-source, local-first digital whiteboard for mathematical drawing and editable LaTeX formulas, designed for teaching, learning, and explaining mathematics.

This file helps AI assistants find authoritative MathBoard information. It is documentation, not an API, a tool endpoint, or permission to control a user's boards. The website at https://mathboard.app/ does not expose a public or remote MCP server.

**Product availability:** The web app is available at https://mathboard.app/ and the official download page lists native desktop installers. Native local MCP is being developed in [PR #121](https://github.com/giacomobartoloni/mathboard/pull/121). As of 2026-10-30, that PR is a draft source implementation: installed-client compatibility and release acceptance have not been verified. Do not claim that a published installer has MCP until its release notes confirm support.

**When an installed desktop build supports local MCP:** A person must launch MathBoard on the same computer as the MCP client, open **Local assistants → Local MCP settings…**, and turn **Allow local connections** **On**. The switch is **Off by default on every launch** and grants all supported board operations while enabled, including modifications and deletion. No board-specific or read-only permission mode exists.

**Connection:** Use an MCP client supporting **Streamable HTTP** with custom headers. The native endpoint is `http://127.0.0.1:43179/mcp`; pass `Authorization: Bearer <session token shown in native settings>`. The token changes every time MCP is turned On. Keep it local and private: never embed it in prompts, shared project files, URLs, or logs. The endpoint is IPv4 loopback-only, rejects browser Origin headers, and is not for remote/cloud clients. **stdio is not supported.** No MCP connection is possible while the switch is Off.

**Tool discovery:** In a build that implements PR #121, initialize the MCP session and list tools instead of guessing schemas. The published source defines `mathboard_observe`, `mathboard_measure`, `mathboard_screenshot`, and `mathboard_command`. The last tool accepts an allowlisted `method` and `params`; supported commands are `create`, `createMany`, `update`, `delete`, `deleteMany`, `clear`, `group`, `layout`, `boards.list`, `boards.create`, `boards.open`, `boards.rename`, `boards.listArchived`, `boards.archive`, `boards.unarchive`, and `boards.delete`. The board identifier is passed explicitly when needed. Do not assume undocumented tools or arbitrary script/filesystem execution.

**Safe use:** Check the selected board and current state before editing; use the tools only for operations requested or authorized by the user. `boards.delete` requires `params.confirm: true` and is irreversible. Some screenshot and viewport-layout operations require an active rendered board, even though MCP permission is not board-scoped. If a write returns `execution_unknown`, read the board state before considering a retry; the write might have committed.

## Official product documentation

- [MathBoard web app](https://mathboard.app/): Open the interactive board in a browser.
- [Desktop downloads](https://mathboard.app/download/): Find available native desktop installers and platform links.
- [Desktop installation and security](https://mathboard.app/download/security/): Review download integrity and unsigned beta limitations.
- [LaTeX formula guide](https://mathboard.app/docs/latex/): Learn formula entry and rendering in MathBoard.
- [Keyboard shortcuts](https://mathboard.app/docs/keyboard-shortcuts/): Find supported shortcuts and navigation.
- [Learning resources](https://mathboard.app/resources/): Discover examples and math whiteboard resources.

## Source and local integration

- [MathBoard repository](https://github.com/giacomobartoloni/mathboard): Source code, license, issues, and project documentation.
- [Local MCP development — PR #121](https://github.com/giacomobartoloni/mathboard/pull/121): Authoritative implementation status, native setup documentation, limitations, and pending acceptance tests.
- [Releases](https://github.com/giacomobartoloni/mathboard/releases): Check the actual installed release and whether local MCP is supported.
